title: Paid early, then the workday
hook: Could wage timing affect output before total pay changes?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Separate short-term liquidity from the total wage and inspect indebtedness as a moderator.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Separate short-term liquidity from the total wage and inspect indebtedness as a moderator.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy worker receives €20 early and €80 later, with a €15 expense due now. What immediate shortfall remains? Toy inputs A=[20, 80, 15]; B=[0, 100, 15].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[100, 0, 20], [100, 15, 0]]. Labels: Total wage €, Immediate shortfall €, Cash now €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The two schedules pay the same total wage but create different immediate liquidity. That timing difference can matter even without a higher lifetime payment. The model exposes the constraint rather than assigning a productivity effect to it.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Paid early €=0, Paid later €=100, Due now €=15. What is Immediate shortfall €? Answer: 15.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Paid early €=0, Paid later €=100, Due now €=15. What is Immediate shortfall €?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 15. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Paying Indian workers part of their wages early raised productivity, especially among the most indebted (Kaur, Mullainathan, Oh & Schilbach, 2021).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Separate short-term liquidity from the total wage and inspect indebtedness as a moderator.
